_readme: HUMAN-AUTHORED FILE. CI NEVER WRITES BACK (ADR-0042 D6). The update protocol — what a re-baseline PR must state — lives in baseline.README.md next to this file. Read it before changing a number here.
_what_these_numbers_are: Hosted-runner (ubuntu-latest) means, in NANOSECONDS, with a per-benchmark tolerance band in PERCENT. They are deliberately NOT the workstation figures published in README.md / docs/README-technical.md (AMD Ryzen 9 9900X, 12C/24T), which are 1.97x-2.35x faster; gating against those would red this job permanently (ADR-0042 D4, Option D). Regression protection is this file's job; document-vs-record correspondence is COHERENCE's (D7). The two are separate failures and are detected separately.

calibration.method: Parsed the BenchmarkDotNet `-report-full-compressed.json` artifacts of 13 real runs of .github/workflows/perf-regression.yml — 12 scheduled (weekly cron) plus 1 workflow_dispatch. `mean_ns` is the mean of those per-run means; the band is set to cover the observed across-run spread with headroom.
calibration.why_the_bands_are_wide: ubuntu-latest alternates between two CPU models and the EPYC 9V74 is uniformly faster — up to 20.7% on some benchmarks. Bands are POOLED across both fleets: one band per benchmark, wide enough for either CPU, because the workflow cannot choose its host. Within-run CV is 0.11%-0.67%; across-run CV is 0.5%-11.2%. This is why a band is NEVER derived from `Statistics.StandardDeviation` in a report — that is the within-run figure and is roughly 20x too tight, and a gate built on it would be red most weeks for reasons that have nothing to do with this repository's code.
calibration.verification: 0 breaches across all 13 runs under these bands; tightest headroom 5.8 percentage points.
calibration.two_sided: Bands are two-sided. The SLOWER side is the regression this gate exists to catch. The FASTER side is a stale-baseline signal (ADR-0042 D6) or a benchmark whose work got optimised away — it is reported as its own kind of breach, not as good news.

sources._comment: artifacts subdirectory (relative to --artifacts-root) -> the BenchmarkDotNet type whose report MUST be there. One row per `--filter` step in .github/workflows/perf-regression.yml. Adding a filter step obliges a row here AND its baseline entries below; a row whose results/ directory or report file is missing is a HARD failure, which is what closes the `|| true` hole (ADR-0042 D4).
